title: The Frostmite That Splits in Three
story: In the blue heart of the Whistlecrag glacier, Volarnix the Trisecting Frostmite guards a frozen sledge full of rescue rope. Mr 6 learns the trap: every time the frostmite is struck, it splits into 3 frostmites — and it starts as a single one. The ice cavern can only hold 90 frostmites before it cracks.
question: If Mr 6 struck every frostmite four times over (four rounds of splitting), how many frostmites would there be?
solution: Round by round the count triples: 1 → 3 → 9 → 27 → 81.
That is 1 x 3 x 3 x 3 x 3 = 81 frostmites.
Four rounds of splitting would make 81 frostmites.
praise: Tripling was the right pattern to spot — one more round of tripling was all that was missing.
hint: Start with 1 and triple it, then triple that answer, keeping track of how many rounds you have done.
victory: Mr 6 sheathed his sword, breathed warm air on the sledge instead, and slid the rope free — and Volarnix, with nobody to split against, curled up as one very confused snowflake. Thinking beat swinging, 81 to nothing.
imagePrompt: A glittering blue ice cavern where a small numeral-six knight lowers his sword thoughtfully before a single spiky frost-insect creature, ghostly outlines of dozens of copies shimmering behind it in the cold light.
